questions.statement: If you ________ water to 100 degrees Celsius, it ________.

options.feedback: Correct! Zero conditional uses Present Simple in both clauses for facts.
Incorrect. This sounds like a specific prediction, but Zero is for general facts.
Incorrect. Subject-verb agreement errors.
Incorrect. This is past tense.

questions.explanation:
El Condicional Cero se usa para hechos científicos o verdades universales. La estructura es: If + Presente Simple, Presente Simple.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If I ________ time this weekend, I ________ to the movies with you.
questions.context: Making a future plan dependent on a condition (First Conditional).

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Will" never goes in the "if" clause.
Correct! First conditional: If + Present Simple, Will + base form.
Incorrect. This is Second Conditional (imaginary).
Incorrect. This would be a general habit, not a specific plan.

questions.explanation:
El Primer Condicional se usa para situaciones reales o muy probables en el futuro. Usamos el Presente Simple después de "if" y "will" en la otra parte.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If you ________ your homework, the teacher ________ angry.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs auxiliary verbs.
Correct! Negative present simple in "if" clause and future in result.
Incorrect. "Will" cannot be in the "if" clause.
Incorrect. "You" takes "don't", not "doesn't".

questions.explanation:
Para formar la parte negativa del condicional, usamos "don't" o "doesn't" en la condición y "won't" en el resultado.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: We will go to the beach ________ it rains.

options.feedback: Incorrect. If it rains, you usually don't go to the beach.
Correct! "Unless" means "if not" or "except if".
Incorrect. This would mean you only go when it is raining.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
"Unless" funciona como "a menos que". Gramaticalmente equivale a decir "if ... not".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If I finish my project early, I ________ go to the park, but I'm not sure.
questions.context: Modal verbs in First Conditional results.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Will" expresses certainty, but the speaker says "I'm not sure".
Correct! "Might" is used in conditionals to show a possibility instead of a certainty.
Incorrect.
Incorrect. This would be an obligation.

questions.explanation:
En lugar de "will", podemos usar otros verbos modales como "might" o "may" en el resultado del condicional para indicar que la consecuencia no es segura, sino solo posible.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If we don't protect the paramos, many Colombian cities ________ water problems in the future.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a prediction for the future.
Correct! First conditional for a real future consequence.
Incorrect. Plural subject.
Incorrect. Not the standard conditional structure.

questions.explanation:
El Primer Condicional es ideal para advertencias sobre el medio ambiente, donde una acción (o falta de acción) hoy tendrá un efecto real mañana.

---
questions.subject: ingles

options.text: If you will study hard, you will pass.
options.feedback: Incorrect. No "will" in the "if" clause.

options.text: You will pass the exam if you study hard.
options.feedback: Correct! The order can be result + if + condition (no comma needed).

options.text: You pass the exam if you will study hard.
options.feedback: Incorrect.

options.text: If you study hard you will pass.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs a comma when "if" starts the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Se puede cambiar el orden de las cláusulas: [Condition], [Result] (con coma) o [Result] [Condition] (sin coma). Nunca se pone "will" en la parte del "if".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
**Sentence A:** If I eat peanuts, I get sick.
**Sentence B:** If I eat those peanuts, I will get sick.

What is the difference?
questions.context: Distinguishing Zero and First conditional by meaning.

options.text: There is no difference in meaning.
options.feedback: Incorrect.

options.text: A is a general allergy (always true); B is a prediction for this specific moment.
options.feedback: Correct! A is Zero Conditional, B is First Conditional.

options.text: A is about the past; B is about the future.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both are in present/future context.

options.text: B is more polite than A.
options.feedback: Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
El Condicional Cero (A) describe una ley general o hábito. El Primer Condicional (B) describe lo que pasará en un caso particular en el futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If you feel dizzy, ________ some water and rest.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A bit long for a direct instruction.
Correct! We can use an imperative in the result clause for instructions.
Incorrect.
Incorrect. "Should" is not followed by "to".

questions.explanation:
En lugar de "will", podemos usar el imperativo (la base del verbo) en la cláusula de resultado para dar instrucciones o consejos directos basados en una condición.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"I **will go (A)** to the university **if (B)** I **will pass (C)** the Saber 11 **exam (D)**."

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the correct result form.
Incorrect. Correct conjunction.
Correct! Error found. We must use Present Simple "pass" after "if".
Incorrect. Correct noun.

questions.explanation:
Uno de los errores más persistentes en B1 es intentar usar el futuro (will) en ambas partes de la oración. La regla gramatical prohíbe el uso de "will" inmediatamente después de "if" en este tipo de oraciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If we continue using plastic bags at the current rate, what is the most logical future result?

options.text: Marine life will suffer even more from pollution.
options.feedback: Correct! Logically and grammatically sound prediction.
Incorrect. Illogical result.

options.text: We would saved the planet yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Tense mismatch (past in future prediction).

options.text: Plastic bags are going to disappeared.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Passive/active confusion and spelling error.

questions.explanation:
Evaluar consecuencias requiere pensamiento crítico y la aplicación correcta del Primer Condicional para expresar probabilidades futuras reales basadas en acciones presentes.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Governments are discussing new taxes on sugar. If these taxes are approved, the price of soda will rise. Consequently..."
questions.context: Selecting the best conclusion for a conditional argument.

options.text: people might consume less sugar and improve their health.
options.feedback: Correct! Follows the logic of cause and effect with a modal of possibility.
Incorrect. Illogical conclusion.

options.text: sugar was very popular in the past.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Irrelevant to the conditional argument.

options.text: the taxes didn't work because they are expensive.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Contradicts the "if ... are approved" future focus.

questions.explanation: Para completar un argumento condicional, el estudiante debe identificar una consecuencia que sea tanto gramaticalmente posible como lógicamente coherente con las premisas dadas.
